payload.objective: Find the molecular mechanism that best explains the loss of function of BTK-p.Arg28His (BTK, UniProt Q06187) and test it with one targeted computational test.
payload.question: For a pathogenic missense variant in an immune-deficiency gene, which molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function, and does a targeted computational test change the conclusion that the starting evidence suggested?

Step 1b COLLECT. Subject: variant_id=BTK-p.Arg28His gene=BTK accession=Q06187 position=28 reference=R alternate=H. Write 10 to 16 evidence items with database record IDs (UniProt, ClinVar, structure databases as returned by tools), 1 to 3 gaps, then hand back.

payload.statement: A downregulating mutation in the BTK PH-TH domain linked to X-linked agammaglobulinemia (R28H) impairs BTK activation at the membrane and in the cytosol by preventing PH-TH dimerization.
payload.strength: primary research article; cited by 2 (Europe PMC)

payload.statement: Molecular dynamics with MM/PBSA binding free energies classified the R28C/H BTK-PH mutants as "functional mutations" affecting Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 binding, as opposed to folding mutations (L11P, S14F, F25S, Y40N).
payload.strength: primary research article; cited by 8 (Europe PMC)

payload.statement: The crystal structure of the BTK PH domain and Btk motif shows that functional XLA mutations cluster at the positively charged end of the PH domain around the predicted phosphatidylinositol binding site, and are proposed to reduce affinity for inositol phosphates and so block membrane translocation; the paper does not single out R28 by name in the abstract.
payload.strength: primary research article; cited by 194 (Europe PMC)

payload.statement: The HIKE motif is a highly conserved candidate PH-domain binding site that occurs in the PH domain of Bruton tyrosine kinase; the abstract does not mention residue 28 specifically.
None of the retrieved records measure binding of R28H-containing BTK-PH to IP4, IP6 or PIP3 experimentally; the only R28H-specific binding result (PMID:24307874) is a molecular dynamics simulation.
payload.why_it_matters: Whether R28H lowers phosphoinositide affinity or acts only through PH-TH dimerization decides which mechanism the Helix model should test.

payload.statement: The retrieved literature does not report whether R28H changes BTK-PH fold stability or cellular expression separately from its effect on dimerization, and no retrieved record compares R28H directly with R28C.
payload.why_it_matters: The simulation classifies R28C/H as functional rather than folding mutations, but that is computational only; a loss-of-function mechanism needs experimental separation of folding from dimerization effects.

payload.summary: Literature collection for BTK p.Arg28His (PH-TH domain, XLA-linked). E1 is the only retrieved experimental statement about R28H itself: it impairs BTK activation by preventing PH-TH dimerization (PMID:38971313). E2 is a simulation-only classification of R28C/H as functional. E3 and E4 give general PH-domain context and do not name R28. G1 and G2 record that no retrieved record measures R28H phosphoinositide binding or folding experimentally.

payload.statement: ClinVar classifies NM_000061.3(BTK):c.83G>A (p.Arg28His) as Pathogenic (criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts; 2 of 4 stars; 8 submissions; last evaluated 2025-02-06) for not provided, X-linked agammaglobulinemia, X-linked agammaglobulinemia with growth hormone deficiency.
payload.strength: criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts (rank 2 of 4, clinvar_review_status)

payload.statement: 39 of 170 experimental structures of Q06187 in the Protein Data Bank observe residue 28.

PDB entry 6TT2 (X-RAY DIFFRACTION, 1.36 Å, deposited 2019-12-23) observes residue 28 of Q06187: The PH domain of Bruton's tyrosine kinase mutant R28C; ligands ZN, MG; the residue is mutated in this entry (R28C).

PDB entry 6TSE (X-RAY DIFFRACTION, 1.41 Å, deposited 2019-12-20) observes residue 28 of Q06187: Crystal Structure of 1-methylindoline-2,3-dione covalently bound to the PH domain of Brut…; ligands MG, 72V, ZN; the residue is mutated in this entry (R28C).

PDB entry 1BTK (X-RAY DIFFRACTION, 1.6 Å, deposited 1997-07-01) observes residue 28 of Q06187: PH DOMAIN AND BTK MOTIF FROM BRUTON'S TYROSINE KINASE MUTANT R28C; ligands ZN; the residue is mutated in this entry (R28C).
PDB entry 7I97 (X-RAY DIFFRACTION, 1.692 Å, deposited 2025-03-24) observes residue 28 of Q06187: Crystal Structure of 8 bound to the PH domain of Btk; ligands MG, ZN, A1B6P.
AlphaFold DB model AF-Q06187-F1 covers the full sequence of Q06187 (mean pLDDT 84.44).
ClinVar lists NM_000061.3(BTK):c.82C>T (p.Arg28Cys) at the same residue as Pathogenic (criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts).
ClinVar lists NM_000061.3(BTK):c.83G>T (p.Arg28Leu) at the same residue as Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic (criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts).
EVE score for p.Arg28His is not covered (state not_covered; value null).
payload.why_it_matters: Only AlphaMissense, ScoreCons and popEVE are available for this substitution, so the computational predictions for R28H rest on three sources, one of which is a proteome-wide scale.

Step 2 HYPOTHESES for BTK-p.Arg28His (Q06187). Read evidence E1-E19 and gaps G1-G4 with read_record. Write at least 2 agent-generated hypotheses of different mechanism classes, each with supporting evidence IDs, a refutation criterion and a starting rank, then hand back. Note UniProt residue calls returned errors, so weight evidence accordingly.

payload.statement: Agent-generated hypothesis: the Arg28His substitution removes an Arg28-mediated contact across the PH-TH dimer interface, so the mutant cannot form the PH-TH dimer needed for membrane-proximal activation of BTK.
payload.would_refute: Residue 28 in experimental structures that contain the PH-TH dimer (or the homodimeric assembly) makes no inter-chain contact within about 5 Å of the partner chain, and the interface is unchanged between wild-type-like and R28C or R28H-like structures.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: E1 is the only record that names R28H and links it to a specific loss-of-function step (PH-TH dimerization blocked at membrane and cytosol). E5, E6 and E9 show strong clinical and predictive pathogenicity but do not name a mechanism. Missing: no direct dimer-interface measurement for R28H (G2), and the structural records are for R28C, not R28H.

payload.statement: Agent-generated hypothesis: the Arg28His substitution removes a positively charged contact that the PH domain uses to bind inositol phosphate or phosphoinositide head groups, reducing membrane recruitment of BTK.
payload.would_refute: In ligand-bound experimental PH-domain structures that observe residue 28, no inositol phosphate, phosphoinositide or phosphate-like ligand lies within about 4.5 Å of the residue 28 side chain, and the residue is not part of the positively charged head-group pocket.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: E2 is the only R28H-specific result pointing to ligand binding (MM/PBSA, Ins(1,3,4,5)P4), but it is a simulation and labels the mutant as functional rather than folding. E3 and E4 place the functional XLA cluster at the phosphoinositide site without naming R28. Conservation and predictor scores (E9 to E11) fit a binding site but do not identify one. Missing: experimental binding data for R28H (G1).

payload.statement: Agent-generated hypothesis: the Arg28His substitution destabilises the PH-domain fold through loss of intramolecular contacts or charge balance at residue 28, lowering folded BTK levels without changing its binding partners directly.
payload.would_refute: The AlphaFold model and experimental structures show residue 28 with no buried intramolecular contact (side chain solvent exposed or contacting only solvent), and the substitution gives a predicted stability change near zero with no change in local backbone dynamics in MD.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: Weakest of the three. E2 classifies R28H as a functional rather than folding mutation, and no record reports folding stability for R28H (G2). The only support is the residue's conservation and the high-confidence AlphaFold model (E10, E17), which are generic. Still kept because G2 leaves stability unexcluded and the record does not test it.

payload.summary: Three agent-generated hypotheses for BTK-p.Arg28His are recorded with distinct mechanism classes: H1 protein_interaction (PH-TH dimer contact lost, rank 1), H2 ligand_binding (inositol phosphate or phosphoinositide head-group contact lost, rank 2), H3 stability_folding (fold destabilised, rank 3). Each has a refutation criterion. Structural records E13 to E16 are for R28C, not R28H, and G1 to G4 remain open, so the test choice should account for these gaps.

Step 3 PLAN for BTK-p.Arg28His. Read hypotheses H1 (protein_interaction, rank 1), H2 (ligand_binding, rank 2), H3 (stability_folding, rank 3) and the test catalogue with read_record. Budget remaining is enforced by policy. Write at least 2 test candidates with expected learning, feasibility and cost, then one plan naming the single chosen test and why each rejected test was rejected, then hand back.

payload.description: Check whether residue 28 of BTK-PH sits next to a bound inositol phosphate, phosphoinositide, or other ligand in the 39 experimental structures that observe it. A contact supports H2 (ligand binding). Structures where residue 28 is itself mutated are reported separately (site-state control), so the wild-type-like set is the one that counts.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A contact with a phosphate-like head group would raise H2 above H1 and H3. Only ligand contacts count, not dimer contacts, so H1 is not moved directly. If no ligand is near residue 28 in the non-mutant structures, H2 drops, but absence of a ligand-bound structure is not evidence of no binding, so the drop is partial. Most of the 39 structures appear to be R28C mutants (6TT2, 6TSE, 1BTK), which the site-state control separates out, so the usable set may be small. That limits the learning.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: list_available_tests reports can_run=true, with 39 structures observing residue 28 and holding a non-solvent ligand. No approval is needed, compute is 0 s, and the cost is 2 tool calls.
controls: Negative control: ligands in the same structures that never list the residue as a neighbour.
Selectivity control: number of distinct residues that neighbour the contacting ligand, so a contact is not an artefact of a large neighbour list.
Site-state control: structures in which the residue itself is mutated are reported separately.

payload.description: FoldX predicted folding free-energy change for R28H on the AlphaFold model (AF-Q06187-F1, mean pLDDT 84.4), together with pLDDT at residue 28 and the same predictor's values for other disease substitutions at residue 28. A strongly destabilising value supports H3 (stability).
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A destabilising value at or above the threshold would raise H3 above H1 and H2. A neutral value would lower H3, which would strengthen the current favourite H1 (the dimer-interface story) by default. The test does not measure dimerisation or ligand binding, so H1 and H2 are not separated by it. FoldX errors are around 1 kcal/mol, so a borderline value would not move the ranking much.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: list_available_tests reports can_run=true and the FoldX state at this substitution as ok. The value is not known until the test runs. No approval, 0 compute seconds, 2 tool calls.
controls: Within-site comparison: the same predictor for the other substitutions reported at this residue.
Applicability control: the model confidence (pLDDT) at the residue, because FoldX on a low-confidence region is not interpretable.

payload.description: Check whether residue 28 lines a predicted pocket (P2Rank on the AlphaFold model, or ProtVar) and whether it lies in a predicted protein-protein interface. A pocket hit weakly supports H2. An interface hit supports H1.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: The H1 arm is weak: ProtVar's interface state for residue 28 is not_covered, so the interface result will probably be empty. The pocket arm only weakly supports H2, and a predicted pocket is not a measured binding site. Both outcomes leave the ranking largely unchanged.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: list_available_tests reports can_run=true. ProtVar pocket data answers for this residue, and P2Rank runs on the AlphaFold model. No approval, 0 compute seconds, 2 tool calls.
controls: Rank control: the rank and probability of the pocket among all predicted pockets of the model.
Confidence control: mean pLDDT of the pocket residues.

payload.description: Predict the reference and R28H construct (residues 1-143) with the same provider and compare local and global C-alpha RMSD, site pLDDT, and contact changes. A confident local rearrangement weakly supports H3.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: Structure predictors are not validated for single-residue substitutions. A matching fold, the likely result for a single substitution, is uninformative. Only a large local rearrangement would move H3, and the test is unlikely to produce one. It does not test H1 or H2.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: The esm_atlas provider cannot run because the UniProt sequence is unavailable, so no construct can be built. Only cached_examples can run, and it performs no new inference and returns an existing result. Approval is required and the test costs 120 compute seconds, about 40% of the remaining 300 s.
controls: Same provider, model version and construct for both sequences.
Residues with low confidence in either model are masked before the RMSD is computed.

The four R28C structures (6TT2, 6TSE, 1BTK, 6YYF) show 0 contacts, but they carry no phosphate-type ligand, so that control cannot show a mutant effect. payload.text:
## Question
Which molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function of BTK p.Arg28His (UniProt Q06187), and does one targeted computational test change the starting conclusion? [E5, E6]

## Evidence
ClinVar classifies the variant as Pathogenic with multiple submitters and no conflicts [E5]. UniProt lists it as a natural variant in X-linked agammaglobulinemia [E6]. Literature reports that R28H impairs PH-TH dimerization [E1] and classes R28C/H as functional rather than folding mutants [E2]. Residue 28 is observed in 39 of 170 experimental structures [E12]. AlphaMissense predicts pathogenicity of 0.9978, a prediction only [E9]. No retrieved record measures R28H binding to inositol phosphates directly [G1], and fold stability is not separated from dimerization [G2].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
H1 (protein interaction at the PH-TH dimer interface) was ranked first [H1]. H2 (ligand binding to the inositol phosphate head-group site) was ranked second [H2]. H3 (fold destabilisation) was ranked third [H3].

## Tests considered and the choice
The planner scored four tests. T1 (ligand contact) was chosen first, with the highest expected learning [T1]. T2 (stability), T3 (structural context) and T4 (structure comparison) were the alternatives [T2, T3, T4]. T3 could not return a positive H1 result because residue 28 is not covered for interface [T3, G3].

## Result
T1 found residue 28 within 4.5 Å of an organic ligand in 32 of 39 ligand-bound structures, closest at 2.58 Å to 4PT in 2Z0P and 2.75 Å to 4IP in 1BWN [T1, E20, E21]. Negative-control ligands never contacted it, and the R28C structures showed no contacts [T1, E22]. This is a distance survey, not a measurement on R28H.

## Updated decision
Before T1, H1 was favoured [H1]. After T1, H2 was favoured and the decision changed [T1, H2]. The reopened round chose T2, a FoldX prediction of −0.76 kcal/mol for R28H, below the 2.0 kcal/mol threshold [T2, E23]. This weakened H3 [H3]. H2 stayed favoured [T2, H2]. H1 is untested, not refuted [H1].

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
The T1 contacts come from wild-type and R28C structures; no R28H structure is in the set [T1, E12]. FoldX has an error of about 1 kcal/mol, so the T2 value is a prediction and not clearly neutral [T2]. Neither the contact nor the stability result has been validated experimentally, and the ligand-binding effect of R28H is unmeasured [G1, H2].

## Next experiment
A laboratory binding measurement for H2: isothermal titration calorimetry or SPR of Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 against wild-type, R28H and R28C PH-TH domains [H2]. Prediction, not yet measured: R28H binds at least 3-fold weaker than wild type [H2]. Binding within about 2-fold of wild type would overturn H2 [H2].
